title: Jobber alternatives for very small home-service teams
summary: Looking for a Jobber alternative? Compare 8 options for small home-service teams based on price, simplicity, field ops, AI, and marketing.
body_markdown:
## Overview


Jobber is popular with small service businesses because it puts quotes, scheduling, invoices, payments, and customer information in one place. But if you have a small team, Jobber may be a more complicated (and expensive) tool than you really need.


Some lean shops just want fast estimates, invoices, and payments. Others are adding techs and need better routing and dispatch. And some are hitting a different wall entirely: the calendar is fine, but the phone keeps ringing while they’re on a job, leads go cold, and marketing gets pushed to the end of the day.


That’s where the alternatives start to separate themselves. Some are lighter than Jobber. Some go deeper into field operations. Others take on more of the front-office or marketing work.


Below, we compare eight Jobber alternatives for owner-operators and very small home-service teams, including what each does best, where it falls short, and what you can expect to pay.


## Topline Pro


Topline Pro handles the same basic work you’d expect from Jobber: customer management, incoming requests, quotes, scheduling, invoices, and payments.


Where the two start to split is marketing.


Jobber gives contractors a solid set of marketing tools, but most sit inside a separate Marketing Suite add-on. Every Topline Pro plan, however, includes a custom website that Topline Pro builds and manages for you, including unlimited updates. SEO content is written and published for you, social posts go out on a set schedule, and review requests can be sent automatically after jobs. On a higher-tier plan, you increase how often that content goes out and add more marketing firepower.


Topline Pro can also help find work that hasn’t reached your inbox yet. Prospect Feed watches for nearby homeowners asking for services like yours and surfaces those opportunities so you can reach out while they’re still looking. Starter gives you a limited view, while Core and Pro include unlimited interactions.


When somebody does reach out, the rest of the system picks up from there. Website leads flow into the Request Pipeline, where the Sales Assistant can collect missing information and photos by text before you quote the work. You can then build the quote, schedule the job, invoice the customer, and collect payment without moving everything into another system.


### Best for


Topline Pro is best for owners who have outgrown word-of-mouth but don’t want SEO, social posts, reviews, and lead follow-up turning into another job they have to do at night.


It’s especially useful for very small teams that need more marketing and front-office help but aren’t ready to put another person on the payroll.


Kenneth Arthur of Arthur Tile & Remodeling described the experience in a Google review: “With just a few questions, they had the most amazing website for our business ready to go.”


### Drawbacks


The done-for-you approach won’t suit every contractor. If you enjoy running your own marketing and want to personally control every website or social update, you may prefer the control of Jobber’s more hands-on tools.


Results also depend on the trade and market, and they take time. A few Topline Pro reviewers say they hoped to see new leads come in faster, so a new website, SEO, or social program shouldn’t be treated like a switch that immediately turns on a full calendar.


### Pricing


- ‍ **Starter Plan** $199/month **‍**
- **Core Plan** $249/month **‍**
- **Pro Plan** $299/month
- Add On: **Sales Assistant** $200/month


## Housecall Pro


Housecall Pro stands out from Jobber because of its dispatching tools.


The office gets a shared visual calendar where dispatchers can drag jobs between technicians as the schedule changes. A live map shows where techs are in the field, so when an emergency call or last-minute job comes in, a dispatcher can see who’s nearby instead of working from the calendar alone.


Housecall Pro also ties more of the field activity back into that dispatch view. Technicians can clock in for the day, tap “On My Way” to record travel time, “Start” to track time on the job, and “Finish” when the work is complete. Those updates keep the office current without somebody having to call each tech for a status check.


Customers stay in the loop automatically, too. An “On My Way” update can trigger an arrival text and tracking link, cutting down on the “Where’s my contractor?” calls that eat up an office manager’s day.


For shops that want to keep a closer eye on the fleet, Housecall Pro also offers optional vehicle tracking alongside employee GPS. That gives the office more visibility into where trucks are and how long techs are spending on the road.


### Best for


Compared with Jobber, Housecall Pro makes the most sense when live dispatching and crew visibility matter more than simply getting jobs onto a schedule.


### Drawbacks


That stronger dispatch setup can get expensive as the team grows. Housecall Pro limits the number of users included on each plan, and adding more people or features can push the monthly bill up quickly.


Some[longtime users](https://www.capterra.com/p/140363/HouseCall-Pro/reviews/?page=2&utm_source=chatgpt.com#:~:text=Various%20aspects%20of%20the%20platform%27s%20layout%20are%20%22updated%22%20frequently%20and%20cause%20issues%20for%20my%20staff%20which%20in%20turn%20increases%20cost%20and%20impacts%20work%20flow.) also say frequent interface changes and occasional bugs have disrupted workflows they were already used to, which is worth considering if your crew values consistency and doesn’t want to relearn the app every time there’s an update.


### Pricing


- No public pricing available. You must engage Workiz’s sales team to get a quote.


## Workiz


Workiz is a solid option for businesses that rely heavily on phone calls. While Jobber has an AI “receptionist” to handle incoming calls, Workiz brings far more capability with “Genius Answering.”


Genius Answering is an AI tool that responds to customers 24/7 across calls, texts, emails, web forms, and other lead sources. It can answer questions about your services or pricing, collect job details, and book, reschedule, or cancel appointments without someone in the office handling every message.


Workiz passes those rescheduling duties off to another AI tool called “Genius Scheduling,” which looks at technician availability, skills, and nearby appointments when suggesting where a new job should go.


Workiz also keeps the office from having to dig through every customer conversation. Its “Call Insights” tool transcribes and summarizes calls, while “Smart Messaging” drafts customer texts and emails. Finally, “Genius Leads” turns incoming service-request messages into leads without somebody copying the information into the CRM by hand.


### Best for


Small service businesses that get a lot of new work by phone or message and want fewer calls, texts, and scheduling decisions landing on the owner or office manager.


It’s especially useful for shops with several technicians where booking a job means figuring out not only when someone is free, but also which tech has the right skills and is already working nearby.


### Drawbacks


Workiz’s most interesting tools can make the final price harder to judge. Genius Scheduling comes with the Pro and Ultimate plans, but Genius Phone, Genius Answering, and Genius Marketing are separate add-ons. Workiz also doesn’t publish dollar pricing for its main plans, so you need to talk to sales to find out what your setup will cost.


Usage costs are a common complaint in reviews. One[2026 G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/workiz/reviews#:~:text=Pricing%20is%20my,the%20added%20cost.) said many new features came with additional charges and specifically disliked that the phone plans charged “by the minute and per text message.” The same reviewer also reported a delay when moving jobs around the schedule and said the Android app lagged behind the iPhone version.


A[Capterra reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/147525/Workiz/reviews/?page=2#:~:text=Unreasonably%20expensive%20system%20%E2%80%93%20CRM%20%2B%20phone%20service%20costs%20around%20%24400%20per%20month.%20The%20phone%20service%20alone%20costs%20%24100%20but%20only%20includes%201%2C500%20SMS%20messages.%20I%20used%20up%20the%20entire%20limit%20in%20two%20weeks%E2%80%94during%20the%20slowest%20season!) raised a similar concern about phone and SMS costs, saying the included 1,500 texts lasted only two weeks during a slow season before per-message charges kicked in.


### Pricing


## Joist


Its focus has traditionally been the money side of a job: build an estimate, get the customer’s approval, collect a deposit, turn the estimate into an invoice, track expenses, and get paid. That makes it a better fit for an owner-operator who doesn’t need dispatch software because they’re the tech, dispatcher, accountant, and janitor.


Joist added Jobs & Scheduling with its new Run plan in August 2026, so you can now keep customer details, estimates, invoices, notes, and scheduled visits together under one job. But it’s still much lighter than Jobber. You can schedule your visits and catch conflicts, but you can’t assign jobs across individual technicians, compare several tech schedules side by side, or optimize routes for a crew.


### Best for


Solo operators and very small contractors who mainly need to estimate jobs, keep track of costs, offer customers financing, and get paid.


### Drawbacks


The low price comes with fewer tools for managing a growing field team.


Joist’s new Run plan can organize jobs and scheduled visits, but it still isn’t built for dispatching technicians, optimizing routes, tracking a crew by GPS, or managing several employees’ schedules. If you reach the point where multiple trucks are moving between jobs every day, Jobber gives you substantially more control.


### Pricing


Joist costs a lot less than Jobber because it isn’t trying to do nearly as much.


- ‍ **Basics** $10/month **‍**
- **Pro** $17/month **‍**
- **Elite** $32/month **‍**
- **Run** $70/month


## ServiceM8


It’s still a full field-service system. Office staff can schedule and dispatch work from a visual board, see where technicians are in the field, and drag jobs onto the right person’s calendar. ServiceM8 can also suggest booking times based on staff availability and travel time, then optimize the route once the day fills up.


ServiceM8 also has strong tools for businesses that service equipment rather than just properties. Its Asset Management add-on lets technicians attach QR codes to customer equipment, pull up the full service history by scanning the code, complete inspection forms, and give customers a portal where they can report problems directly.


### Best for


Seasonal or lower-volume service businesses with several employees who all need access to the system but don’t want software costs to rise with headcount.


It’s particularly well-suited to trades that need flexible scheduling windows, field checklists, asset histories, or detailed job records, such as HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, pest control, and pool service.


### Drawbacks


The biggest limitation is device support.


ServiceM8 is still heavily Apple-first. Its full mobile experience is designed around iPhone and iPad, while Android users get ServiceM8 Lite, which handles core field tasks but doesn’t include the full feature set available on iOS.


The other tradeoff is the job-credit model. Unlimited users sound great, but what you pay depends on job volume. A contractor with five employees and 40 new jobs a month may come out ahead. A high-volume service shop creating hundreds of one-off jobs can burn through those credits much faster, making the monthly cost less predictable.


### Pricing


ServiceM8 takes a very different approach to pricing than Jobber.


Instead of charging more as you add employees, ServiceM8’s paid plans include unlimited users. Your plan mainly depends on how many new jobs you create each month. That can work well for a small crew where several people need access to the software, but the business doesn’t process hundreds of new service calls every month.


- ‍ **Free** $0/month **‍**
- **Starter** $29/month **‍**
- **Growing** $79/month **‍**
- **Premium** $149/month **‍**
- **Premium Plus** $349/month


## QuoteIQ


QuoteIQ covers much of the same ground as Jobber, including estimates, invoices, scheduling, payments, customer management, time tracking, dispatching, and crew management on its higher plans.


Where it gets more interesting is how contractors build the estimate in the first place.


MapMeasure Pro sits directly inside QuoteIQ’s estimate builder. Enter the property address, and it pulls up satellite imagery, then you can measure roofs, lawns, driveways, fences, and other surfaces without making a separate site visit. AI AutoMeasure can trace a roof, lawn, or driveway automatically, while manual tools let you measure odd shapes or linear footage yourself. For roofing work, it can also detect roof pitch and use that to calculate surface area before you price the job.


That gives QuoteIQ a clear advantage over Jobber for trades where square footage or linear footage drives the estimate. A landscaper can measure a lawn, a pressure washer can size up a driveway, and a roofer can work from the roof dimensions without juggling a separate measuring app and CRM.


QuoteIQ also has another unusual estimating tool: InstaQuote, which lets homeowners build their own estimate before they ever talk to you. You choose which services customers can quote, set the pricing rules and add-ons, then embed the tool on your website or share it by link. Customers enter the job details, see a price based on the rules you set, and can move straight into booking.


### Best for


Roofers, landscapers, painters, pressure washers, concrete contractors, fencing companies, and other trades where measuring the property is a big part of building the quote.


### Drawbacks


A lot of QuoteIQ’s more distinctive features don’t come with the cheapest plan. MapMeasure Pro and QuoteIQ Cam start on Beginner, while InstaQuote, route optimization, inventory, dispatching, and EmployeeHub require Elite or higher.


Its AI tools also run on monthly IQ Credits: AutoPilot commands, AI estimates, virtual-call minutes, image generation, and other AI actions all draw from the same allowance. Plans currently include between 500 and 8,000 credits per month, and unused credits reset rather than rolling over.


There’s much less independent review history for QuoteIQ than for Jobber. That doesn’t mean the product is weak, but it gives a buyer less third-party evidence about how the platform holds up as a business grows.


### Pricing


- ‍ **Essentials** $29/month **‍**
- **Beginner** $74/month **‍**
- **Pro** $149/month **‍**
- **Elite** $299/month **‍**
- **Max** $699/month


## ServiceAgent


Jobber gives you software for running the business, with select AI tools, such as its Receptionist. ServiceAgent is trying to create an AI experience that works like an office manager you can talk to.


Instead of clicking through the CRM to update records, find old leads, send an invoice, or schedule follow-up, ServiceAgent lets you tell its CRM agent what you want done in plain English. Its other AI agents handle different parts of the business, including call answering, appointment scheduling, customer follow-up, billing, marketing, and business reporting.


ServiceAgent claims each of its AI models has been trained specifically for an individual trade, whether that’s HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, solar, cleaning, or a garage-door business. The idea is that the AI answering a call or working inside the CRM needs to understand the difference between a tune-up, emergency leak, panel upgrade, roof inspection, or garage-door repair.


### Best for


Very small home-service businesses where the owner is still wearing the hats of receptionist, office manager, collections person, marketer, and analyst.


It makes the most sense when reducing office work matters more than having the deepest dispatching, routing, or crew-management system.


### Drawbacks


ServiceAgent is much newer than Jobber, and there’s far less independent review history available to show how well the broader platform holds up in day-to-day use.


Some of its bigger ambitions are also still being built. ServiceAgent currently labels several marketing features as coming soon, so the website describes a broader vision than what every customer can use today.


### Pricing


ServiceAgent also uses a credit model. Its paid plans include a monthly pool of credits, and the platform consumes those credits when AI agents take actions for you. That makes the entry price low, but businesses using the agents heavily need to watch usage rather than comparing the subscription price alone.


- ‍ **Launch** $0/month **‍**
- **Core** $39/month **‍**
- **Growth** $95/month **‍**
- **Franchise** $279/month


## Houzz Pro


Houzz Pro handles familiar business tasks like estimates, proposals, change orders, invoices, payments, scheduling, time tracking, and client communication. But Houzz Pro goes after remodelers and builders with deeper project planning tools.


That starts with 3D Floor Plans. Remodelers and designers can scan a room or work from an existing floor plan, build the space to scale, add walls, doors, windows, finishes, furniture, and fixtures, then show the homeowner the project in 2D, 3D, or walkthrough views. Houzz Pro can also generate photorealistic renders and use products saved in the contractor’s product library inside the design.


Its Takeoffs tool tackles another part of preconstruction. You can upload PDF plans, set the scale, measure lengths, areas, volumes, and quantities directly on the drawing, then carry those measurements into an estimate instead of doing the takeoff in separate software.


Houzz Pro also puts a lot more emphasis on product selections and client approvals. A remodeler can use the Product Clipper to save cabinets, tile, fixtures, flooring, furniture, and other products from supplier websites. Houzz Pro pulls in details, such as photos, pricing, dimensions, SKUs, and specifications, and saves them to a reusable product library. Those products can then move into mood boards, 3D plans, estimates, proposals, purchase orders, and client Selection Boards.


### Best for


Remodelers, general contractors, builders, kitchen-and-bath contractors, flooring companies, and design-build businesses selling larger projects where plans, product selections, client approvals, and materials all need to come together before construction begins.


It’s especially useful when showing the homeowner what the finished project will look like is part of winning the job.


### Drawbacks


Houzz Pro is much more specialized than Jobber.


If you run a plumbing, HVAC, pest control, cleaning, or other service business that mainly sends technicians to several short appointments each day, tools like 3D floor plans, mood boards, selections, takeoffs, and product sourcing are likely irrelevant to your work.


### Pricing


- No public pricing available. You must engage with a Houzz Pro sales rep and see a demo first.


## Compare the best Jobber alternatives for small teams


The right Jobber alternative depends on whether you’re trying to get more work, better manage a crew, keep costs down, or take admin off your plate. Here’s the quick side-by-side.


Tool Best for Drawbacks Pricing

Housecall Pro Small crews managing techs, routes, and trucks Costs climb as your crew grows: Essentials includes five users, but additional users cost $100/month each; Max includes eight, then charges $75 per additional user Starts at $59/month


Workiz Small service shops that get a lot of work by phone and want help answering calls and texting customers Some reviewers complain about phone/SMS costs and usage limits No public pricing available


Joist Shops that just need basic estimates, invoices, and payments While simple, Joist offers less depth for managing bigger projects and crews Starts at $8.34/month


ServiceM8 Seasonal or lower-volume contractors who don't want to pay by the employee The full mobile experience is only for iOS; Android users get ServiceM8 Lite, which lacks some of the functionality available on iOS Free tier available


QuoteIQ Contractors who quote based on property measurements Heavy use of estimating, Autopilot, calls, or other AI features can burn through AI credit allowance, and unused credits don’t roll over Starts at $25/month


ServiceAgent Businesses who want AI for answering calls and handling front-office follow-up Its site still says the platform is “launching soon”; there are few independent reviews available online Free tier available
